Chapter 3: Turning Ordinary Activities into Acts of Devotion
Let’s dive into something that can truly change the way you move through your day.
Imagine if every single part of your life—even the most routine things—could become a way to connect with God. What if devotion wasn’t just reserved for special moments or sacred spaces, but could actually weave its way into every chore, every responsibility, every little task you take on?
Here’s the heart of it: it all comes down to intentionality. When you decide to dedicate those everyday moments—like washing dishes, folding laundry, or making dinner—to God, they start to mean so much more.
Suddenly, it’s not just about the task in front of you. It’s about focusing on the One who’s present with you, right in the middle of it all.
And here’s something to pay attention to—this isn’t about adding more to your already full plate. It’s about shifting your attention. Instead of seeing daily duties as things that pull you away from spiritual growth, you can actually turn them into the very space where you grow closer to God.
Let me give you a simple way to try this:
Before you start any activity, take a moment to pause and recognize God’s presence.
Offer what you’re about to do—no matter how small—as an act of love or service.
And then, as you go, stay open to little sparks of gratitude, patience, or even joy that might pop up along the way.
You don’t need to change your whole routine, or invent a bunch of new rituals. It’s really about bringing a sense of purpose and connection to whatever’s in front of you. Over time, you’ll notice that your ordinary moments start to feel a little more sacred, and the line between what’s spiritual and what’s just “daily life” gets a little blurrier.
Of course, challenges will pop up. You’ll probably face boredom, frustration, or wonder if some tasks are just too trivial to matter. But here’s the secret—those moments are actually opportunities. When you invite God into your struggles, even the tough or annoying parts of life can be transformed. Choosing patience when you’re frustrated, or finding gratitude in the middle of something tedious, becomes its own kind of worship.
Another gift of this practice is humility. When you realize that every single task—even the smallest—can be offered to God, it shifts your focus from chasing big achievements to appreciating the dignity and value found in everyday life.
Over time, this way of living weaves faith and action together. Spirituality won’t just belong to special occasions—it becomes a steady, unbroken thread running through everything you do. And as that happens, you’ll feel a deeper sense of connection, purpose, and yes—even joy—in the most ordinary moments of your day.
